description:
Six OID constants in this PR are hand-declared with ObjectIdentifier::new_unwrap() literals instead of importing from const_oid::db, which is already in pkix-chain's transitive dep graph (via der/x509-cert/const-oid 0.9.6):

  - aia_extract.rs:27 OID_AUTHORITY_INFO_ACCESS  '1.3.6.1.5.5.7.1.1' → const_oid::db::rfc5280::ID_PE_AUTHORITY_INFO_ACCESS
  - aia_extract.rs:33 OID_AD_CA_ISSUERS         '1.3.6.1.5.5.7.48.2' → const_oid::db::rfc5280::ID_AD_CA_ISSUERS
  - lib.rs:1318       OID_OCSP_NO_CHECK         '1.3.6.1.5.5.7.48.1.5' → const_oid::db::rfc6960::ID_PKIX_OCSP_NOCHECK
  - lib.rs:1417       OID_EXTENDED_KEY_USAGE    '2.5.29.37' → const_oid::db::rfc5280::ID_CE_EXT_KEY_USAGE
  - lib.rs:1419       ID_KP_TIME_STAMPING       '1.3.6.1.5.5.7.3.8' → const_oid::db::rfc5280::ID_KP_TIME_STAMPING
  - lib.rs:1495       OID_KEY_USAGE             '2.5.29.15' → const_oid::db::rfc5280::ID_CE_KEY_USAGE

Confirmed against the const-oid 0.9.6 source (db/gen.rs). pkix-profiles/src/lib.rs:167 already declares ID_KP_TIME_STAMPING with the same dotted string, so the workspace is now carrying the same OID literal in three places (pkix-profiles, pkix-chain/lib.rs, and would-be-fourth if any other crate adds one).

What goes wrong with hand-redefinition:
  (1) literal duplication invites OID typos that won't be caught by the type system (const ObjectIdentifier::new_unwrap is checked at compile time but produces a 'wrong-OID compiles fine' result, not a build break);
  (2) grep across the workspace for 'who uses id-kp-timeStamping?' returns the literal string rather than a canonical symbol — refactors get harder;
  (3) when const-oid 1.0 ships and the workspace migrates, six call sites need updating instead of one import path.

Idiomatic Rust convention for RustCrypto-formats consumers is to import from const_oid::db::* (or, equivalently, x509_cert::ext::pkix::*::oid where re-exported), then use the named constant. Hand-defining a private const with the same dotted string is the same anti-pattern as redefining E in std::f64 inside your own module.

Cost-cheap fix: replace the 6 const declarations with use statements. Existing match-arm syntax (e.g. 'if *oid == ID_KP_TIME_STAMPING') works unchanged because both sides are ObjectIdentifier.
title: OID constants hand-redefined; const_oid::db::rfc5280/rfc6960 already supplies all six
